subject: Tenant-scoped temporary log preservation request — StellarHealth
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for investigation

Hi Hannah,

We're working through a security incident involving one of our clinics (tenant ID: TH-432). Our internal IR team needs a time-bounded preservation of all request and inference logs tied to that tenant for the window 2028-03-20 — 2028-03-27 while we conduct timeline reconstruction and root-cause analysis.

Questions we have up front:
- Can Redwood put a tenant-scoped preservation/hold in place so normal TTL/housekeeping does not delete the logs for that tenant?
- Can you provide a brief description of the process and the expected time-to-evidence (how long until we can get a tamper-evident snapshot)?
- What artifacts can you provide to demonstrate the hold and subsequent deletion (if any) for SOC 2 / SIG review?

We understand retention-hold requests are exceptional; we're happy to sign an acknowledgment and cover reasonable operational costs. Please loop in whoever owns log custody.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Security Operations
StellarHealth

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for investigation

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. I've looped in Marissa (Support lead for Compliance) and Karthik (Platform / retention owner) to coordinate the technical hold and evidence pack. High-level answers below; we'll follow with a concrete plan and timeframe by EOD.

Short answers:
- Yes — we can apply a tenant-scoped preservation. We create a logical hold that prevents automated deletion for the specified tenant and time window; this is enforced at the service layer and backed by immutable audit logs.
- ETA: we can produce a tamper-evident snapshot and preliminary index within 24–48 hours of a confirmed request; full packaged evidence (checksums + manifest) within 72 hours.
- Artifacts: manifest CSV with object keys and timestamps, SHA256 checksums, an audit log extract showing the hold action (who/when), and a deletion attest (signed by Redwood Operations) when the hold is cleared.

To proceed we need:
1) Confirm tenant ID(s) and exact date ranges (you listed TH-432 / 2028-03-20 — 2028-03-27).
2) Confirmation that StellarHealth will accept a temporary export and retention under the joint-preservation agreement (I can share a short acceptance template).
3) Any additional scope (e.g., include metadata / KV cache snapshots) — those increase collection time.

I'm attaching a standard redwood_log_hold_template.docx that documents the acceptance language we use for SIG/SOC2 reviewers. Karthik — can you confirm backend steps and whether we need a scheduled job to pin S3 objects for this tenant?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_log_hold_template.docx (template: short acceptance + retention/clearance checklist)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2028-04-05T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for investigation

Thanks Hannah — confirming:
- Tenant: TH-432 (single tenant)
- Window: 2028-03-20 00:00:00 UTC to 2028-03-27 23:59:59 UTC
- Scope: request+response logs, inference traces, and request-level metadata (no raw customer payload dumps)

We accept the joint-preservation agreement; I've signed the acceptance (see attached S3 path list — it's just sample ids, we'll provide the full list if you need it). A couple of follow-ups:
1) For SOC 2 evidence we need a clear chain-of-custody: who performed the hold, when it was applied, and an audit extract showing no modifications after apply. Will that be in the audit log extract you mentioned?
2) After the investigation, we need a deletion certificate proving artifacts were removed according to the agreed schedule. Can Redwood produce a signed deletion attest with object-level checksums?

Attached: S3-paths-and-sample-ids.txt (sample object keys from our side).

—Daniel

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-06T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary preservation of tenant logs for investigation

Hi Daniel — good to confirm scope. Below is the operational plan and deliverables we will provide. Please review and sign off so we can execute.

Operational plan (timeline and outputs):
- T+0 (within 4 hours of your sign-off): create tenant-scoped hold in the control plane. This action is recorded in our immutable audit stream and will be visible to you in the shared audit extract.
- T+24–48 hours: produce an index (CSV) of all objects matching TH-432 for 2028-03-20 — 2028-03-27. The CSV will include: object_key, created_at, size_bytes, and SHA256 checksum. (See sample column layout attached.)
- T+72 hours: full evidence pack (evidence-pack-logs-20280406.zip) containing:
  - retention-snapshot-tenant-432.csv (manifest)
  - platform-audit-extract.jsonl (append-only audit lines showing hold apply, access events, and no mutations)
  - checksums.txt (SHA256 for each object)
  - chain_of_custody.txt (who performed each action + UTC timestamps)

Chain-of-custody and tamper evidence:
- The hold action is a single write to our governance table; that write is replicated to an immutable ledger and included in the audit extract. Each object included in the manifest will have an SHA256 checksum generated at snapshot time and included in checksums.txt.
- For SOC 2/SIG reviewers we can provide redacted extracts of the immutable ledger and a signed deletion certificate once the hold is cleared. The deletion certificate contains object keys, checksums, deletion timestamps, and a Redwood Ops signature (PGP-signed metadata).

Post-investigation cleanup options (choose one):
A) Automatic deletion after a fixed retention (we'll remove all preserved objects 30 days after the hold is cleared).
B) Manual deletion after your written authorization + Redwood deletion certificate.

Costs: there is a small operational fee for on-demand evidence packaging and long-term object pinning; Marissa will provide a quote in a separate note.

Next steps:
1) Reply to this thread with explicit sign-off on the operational plan and chosen cleanup option (A or B).
2) We will create the hold and send the first index within 24 hours.

If helpful for auditors, we can also schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with our compliance engineer to review the artifacts and the chain-of-custody formatting.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Manager, Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention-snapshot-tenant-432.csv (manifest sample), evidence-pack-logs-20280406.zip (placeholder for final evidence pack)
